# Requirements Specification: YAML Validator Command

**Feature ID**: yaml-validator-command
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-01-22

## 1. Feature Overview

A command-line utility that validates YAML file syntax by parsing files specified via command-line arguments. The validator uses a custom-built minimal YAML parser implemented from scratch, ensuring no new external dependencies are added to the project. This tool enables developers to quickly verify that their YAML configuration files are syntactically correct before deployment or further processing.

## 2. Business Context

### 2.1 Problem Statement

Developers working with YAML configuration files need a quick way to validate file syntax without relying on external dependencies. Invalid YAML files can cause runtime errors, deployment failures, or configuration issues that are difficult to debug. Currently, there is no built-in mechanism to validate YAML syntax within the existing toolset.

### 2.2 Business Value

- Reduces debugging time by catching YAML syntax errors early in the development workflow
- Maintains project simplicity by avoiding additional npm dependencies
- Provides developers with immediate feedback on configuration file validity
- Prevents deployment failures caused by malformed YAML files

### 2.3 Success Metrics

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Correctly identifies valid YAML files | 100% accuracy for supported syntax |
| Correctly identifies invalid YAML files | Clear error messaging with line numbers |
| Command execution time | Less than 500ms for typical config files |
| No new dependencies added | Zero new npm packages |

## 3. Stakeholders & Users

### 3.1 User Types

| User Type | Description | Primary Needs |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| Developer | Team members using CLI tools for development workflow | Quick syntax validation, clear error messages, simple invocation |

### 3.2 Stakeholder Interests

| Stakeholder | Interest |
|-------------|----------|
| Development Team | Maintain codebase simplicity, no dependency bloat |
| Project Maintainers | Ensure tool reliability and minimal maintenance burden |

## 4. Scope Definition

### 4.1 In Scope

- Command-line interface accepting file path argument
- Custom YAML parser implementation (no external dependencies)
- Syntax validation (parse success/failure)
- Clear success/failure output messages
- Line number reporting for syntax errors
- Support for common YAML syntax constructs (scalars, mappings, sequences, comments)

### 4.2 Out of Scope

- YAML schema validation (e.g., validating against a JSON Schema)
- YAML linting or style checking
- YAML formatting or pretty-printing
- Multiple file validation in single command
- Stdin input support
- YAML anchors and aliases
- Multi-document YAML files
- Complex YAML features (tags, custom types, binary data)

### 4.3 Assumptions

- Developers have access to the CLI environment (Bun runtime)
- YAML files are encoded in UTF-8
- Target files are single-document YAML files
- Files are of reasonable size (under 10MB)

## 5. Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: File Path Input
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Must Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The command shall accept a file path as a command-line argument |
| Rationale | Developers need to specify which file to validate |
| Acceptance Criteria | Running `bun run validate config.yaml` passes the file path to the validator |

### REQ-002: File Existence Check
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Must Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The command shall verify the specified file exists before attempting validation |
| Rationale | Clear error messaging prevents confusion when files are missing |
| Acceptance Criteria | Non-existent file paths produce a clear "file not found" error message |

### REQ-003: YAML Syntax Parsing
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Must Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The command shall parse YAML content using a custom-built parser without external dependencies |
| Rationale | Project constraint requires no new npm dependencies |
| Acceptance Criteria | Parser correctly handles scalars, key-value mappings, lists, nested structures, and comments |

### REQ-004: Success Output
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Must Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The command shall output a success message when the YAML file is syntactically valid |
| Rationale | Developers need confirmation that validation passed |
| Acceptance Criteria | Valid YAML files produce output indicating success (e.g., "Valid YAML") |

### REQ-005: Error Output with Location
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Must Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The command shall output an error message including line number when syntax errors are detected |
| Rationale | Line numbers help developers quickly locate and fix errors |
| Acceptance Criteria | Invalid YAML produces error message with line number (e.g., "Syntax error at line 15: ...") |

### REQ-006: Exit Codes
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Should Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The command shall return appropriate exit codes (0 for success, non-zero for failure) |
| Rationale | Enables integration with scripts and CI/CD pipelines |
| Acceptance Criteria | Exit code 0 on valid YAML, exit code 1 on invalid YAML or errors |

### REQ-007: No New Dependencies
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Must Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The implementation shall not add any new npm packages to the project |
| Rationale | Project constraint to maintain minimal dependencies |
| Acceptance Criteria | package.json dependencies remain unchanged after implementation |

## 6. Non-Functional Requirements

### 6.1 Performance Expectations

| Requirement | Target |
|-------------|--------|
| Validation time for files under 100KB | Less than 100ms |
| Validation time for files under 1MB | Less than 500ms |
| Memory usage | Proportional to file size, no memory leaks |

### 6.2 Security Requirements

| Requirement | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| File access | Only read access to specified file path |
| Path traversal | Handle file paths safely without arbitrary file system access |

### 6.3 Usability Requirements

| Requirement | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| Error clarity | Error messages must be human-readable and actionable |
| Help text | Command should provide usage information when invoked incorrectly |
| Output format | Consistent, parseable output format |

### 6.4 Compliance Requirements

None identified for this feature.

## 7. User Stories

### STORY-001: Validate a YAML Configuration File
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Story | As a Developer, I want to validate a YAML configuration file so that I can ensure it will parse correctly before deployment |
| Acceptance | GIVEN a valid YAML file exists at "config.yaml" WHEN I run `bun run validate config.yaml` THEN I see a success message confirming the file is valid |

### STORY-002: Identify Syntax Errors
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Story | As a Developer, I want to see where syntax errors occur so that I can quickly fix malformed YAML |
| Acceptance | GIVEN a YAML file with a syntax error on line 10 WHEN I run the validate command THEN I see an error message indicating the problem at line 10 |

### STORY-003: Handle Missing Files
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Story | As a Developer, I want clear feedback when a file does not exist so that I can correct the file path |
| Acceptance | GIVEN no file exists at "missing.yaml" WHEN I run `bun run validate missing.yaml` THEN I see an error message stating the file was not found |

### STORY-004: Script Integration
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Story | As a Developer, I want the command to return proper exit codes so that I can use it in automated scripts |
| Acceptance | GIVEN a valid YAML file WHEN the validate command completes THEN the exit code is 0 AND GIVEN an invalid YAML file WHEN the validate command completes THEN the exit code is non-zero |

## 8. Business Rules

| Rule ID | Rule | Rationale |
|---------|------|-----------|
| BR-001 | The validator must use only built-in language features and existing project code | Maintains zero-dependency constraint |
| BR-002 | Syntax validation only; no semantic or schema validation | Keeps scope minimal and implementation simple |
| BR-003 | Single file per invocation | Simplifies implementation and usage |

## 9. Dependencies & Constraints

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| Bun runtime | Runtime | Command executes in Bun environment |
| File system access | System | Read access to validate target files |

### Constraints

| Constraint | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| No new npm dependencies | Implementation must use only existing packages and built-in features |
| Custom parser | YAML parsing must be implemented from scratch |
| Syntax-only validation | No schema or semantic validation required |

## 10. Clarifications Log

| Question | Clarification | Source |
|----------|---------------|--------|
| Who are the target users? | Developers via CLI | User clarification |
| How is input provided? | File path as command argument | User clarification |
| What level of validation? | Syntax only - check if YAML parses correctly | User clarification |
| Which YAML parser to use? | Custom minimal parser implemented from scratch | User clarification |

---

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Defaults

| Decision Point | Choice | Rationale |
|----------------|--------|-----------|
| PRD selection | None | No PRDs found in .rp1/work/prds/ directory |
| KB context | Best-effort without KB | index.md and concept_map.md not found |

## AFK Mode: Inferred Decisions

| Ambiguity | Resolution | Source |
|-----------|------------|--------|
| Supported YAML features | Basic syntax: scalars, mappings, sequences, comments | Conservative default for "simple" validator |
| Error reporting format | Line number with descriptive message | Standard practice for CLI validators |
| Exit code convention | 0 for success, 1 for failure | Unix convention default |
| File size limits | Reasonable files under 10MB | Conservative default assumption |
| Encoding support | UTF-8 only | Most common YAML encoding |
| Multi-document support | Out of scope | "Simple" validator constraint |
| Advanced YAML features | Out of scope (anchors, aliases, tags) | Custom minimal parser constraint |

# Technical Design: YAML Validator Command

**Feature ID**: yaml-validator-command
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-01-22

---

## 1. Design Overview

This design specifies a command-line YAML syntax validator for the rp1-eval-project. The validator accepts a file path argument, parses the YAML content using a custom-built parser, and reports success or failure with appropriate error messages and exit codes.

### High-Level Architecture

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph CLI["CLI Layer"]
        A[validate.ts]
    end

    subgraph Parser["Parser Layer"]
        B[yaml-parser.ts]
    end

    subgraph System["System Layer"]
        C[File System]
        D[Process/Exit]
    end

    A --> B
    A --> C
    A --> D
    B --> E[YamlLexer]
    B --> F[YamlParser]
```

**Design Principles:**
- Single responsibility: Separate CLI handling from parsing logic
- Zero dependencies: All parsing logic implemented from scratch
- Pattern alignment: Follow existing project structure and conventions

---

## 2. Architecture

### 2.1 Component Structure

| Component | File | Responsibility |
|-----------|------|----------------|
| CLI Entry Point | `src/validate.ts` | Argument parsing, file I/O, output formatting |
| YAML Parser | `src/yaml-parser.ts` | Lexical analysis and parsing of YAML content |

### 2.2 Component Interaction

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant CLI as validate.ts
    participant FS as File System
    participant Parser as yaml-parser.ts

    User->>CLI: bun run validate config.yaml
    CLI->>CLI: Parse arguments
    CLI->>FS: Check file exists
    alt File not found
        CLI->>User: Error: File not found
        CLI->>CLI: exit(1)
    end
    CLI->>FS: Read file contents
    CLI->>Parser: parseYaml(content)
    alt Parse success
        Parser->>CLI: { success: true, data }
        CLI->>User: Valid YAML
        CLI->>CLI: exit(0)
    else Parse failure
        Parser->>CLI: { success: false, error, line }
        CLI->>User: Syntax error at line N: message
        CLI->>CLI: exit(1)
    end
```

---

## 3. Detailed Design

### 3.1 YAML Parser Module (`src/yaml-parser.ts`)

The custom YAML parser implements a two-phase approach: lexical analysis followed by parsing.

#### 3.1.1 Supported YAML Syntax

| Syntax Element | Example | Supported |
|----------------|---------|-----------|
| Scalar values | `key: value` | Yes |
| Quoted strings | `key: "value"` or `key: 'value'` | Yes |
| Multi-line strings | `key: \|` or `key: >` | Yes |
| Numbers | `count: 42` | Yes |
| Booleans | `enabled: true` | Yes |
| Null values | `value: null` or `value: ~` | Yes |
| Mappings (objects) | `key:\n  nested: value` | Yes |
| Sequences (arrays) | `- item1\n- item2` | Yes |
| Inline sequences | `items: [a, b, c]` | Yes |
| Inline mappings | `obj: {key: value}` | Yes |
| Comments | `# comment` | Yes |
| Anchors/Aliases | `&anchor`, `*alias` | No |
| Tags | `!tag` | No |
| Multi-document | `---` separator | No |

#### 3.1.2 Parser Interface

```typescript
// Types
interface YamlParseSuccess {
  success: true;
  data: YamlValue;
}

interface YamlParseError {
  success: false;
  error: string;
  line: number;
  column?: number;
}

type YamlParseResult = YamlParseSuccess | YamlParseError;

type YamlValue =
  | string
  | number
  | boolean
  | null
  | YamlValue[]
  | { [key: string]: YamlValue };

// Main function
function parseYaml(content: string): YamlParseResult;
```

#### 3.1.3 Lexer Design

The lexer tokenizes YAML input into a stream of tokens:

```typescript
enum TokenType {
  KEY,           // key identifier before colon
  COLON,         // :
  STRING,        // quoted or unquoted string value
  NUMBER,        // numeric value
  BOOLEAN,       // true/false
  NULL,          // null/~
  DASH,          // - for list items
  LBRACKET,      // [
  RBRACKET,      // ]
  LBRACE,        // {
  RBRACE,        // }
  COMMA,         // ,
  PIPE,          // | for literal block
  GT,            // > for folded block
  NEWLINE,       // line break
  INDENT,        // indentation increase
  DEDENT,        // indentation decrease
  EOF,           // end of file
}

interface Token {
  type: TokenType;
  value: string;
  line: number;
  column: number;
}
```

#### 3.1.4 Parser State Machine

The parser maintains a state stack for handling nested structures:

```typescript
interface ParserState {
  indent: number;       // Current indentation level
  context: 'root' | 'mapping' | 'sequence' | 'inline-mapping' | 'inline-sequence';
  expectingValue: boolean;
}
```

### 3.2 CLI Entry Point (`src/validate.ts`)

#### 3.2.1 Command Interface

```
Usage: bun run validate <file-path>

Arguments:
  file-path    Path to the YAML file to validate

Exit Codes:
  0            YAML file is valid
  1            Validation failed or error occurred
```

#### 3.2.2 CLI Implementation Structure

```typescript
// Main entry point
async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2);

  // Validate arguments
  if (args.length === 0) {
    printUsage();
    process.exit(1);
  }

  const filePath = args[0];

  // Check file existence
  if (!await fileExists(filePath)) {
    console.error(`Error: File not found: ${filePath}`);
    process.exit(1);
  }

  // Read file
  const content = await readFile(filePath);

  // Parse YAML
  const result = parseYaml(content);

  // Output result
  if (result.success) {
    console.log(`Valid YAML: ${filePath}`);
    process.exit(0);
  } else {
    console.error(`Syntax error at line ${result.line}: ${result.error}`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
```

#### 3.2.3 Error Message Formats

| Scenario | Output Format |
|----------|---------------|
| No arguments | `Usage: bun run validate <file-path>` |
| File not found | `Error: File not found: {path}` |
| Valid YAML | `Valid YAML: {path}` |
| Syntax error | `Syntax error at line {N}: {message}` |

### 3.3 Data Model

No persistent data storage required. The parser produces an in-memory representation that is discarded after validation.

---

## 4. Technology Stack

| Layer | Technology | Justification |
|-------|------------|---------------|
| Runtime | Bun | Project standard (existing) |
| Language | TypeScript | Project standard (existing) |
| File I/O | Bun built-in fs | No external dependencies |
| Testing | bun:test | Project standard (existing) |

---

## 5. Implementation Plan

| # | Component | Description | Effort |
|---|-----------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | YAML Parser Core | Implement lexer and parser in `src/yaml-parser.ts` | Medium |
| 2 | CLI Entry Point | Implement `src/validate.ts` with argument handling | Small |
| 3 | Package.json Update | Add "validate" script | Trivial |

---

## 6. Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1] - YAML parser has no dependencies on other new components
2. [T2] - CLI entry point depends on parser being complete
3. [T3] - Package.json update depends on CLI entry point

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (Interface dependency: CLI imports and uses parseYaml function)
- T3 -> T2 (Build dependency: Script references validate.ts entry point)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2 -> T3

---

## 7. Testing Strategy

### 7.1 Test Value Assessment

| Test Category | Value | Rationale |
|---------------|-------|-----------|
| Parser unit tests | HIGH | Core business logic - validates YAML syntax |
| CLI integration tests | MEDIUM | Verifies end-to-end behavior |
| Edge case tests | HIGH | YAML has many syntax variations |

### 7.2 Test Plan

#### 7.2.1 Parser Unit Tests (`src/yaml-parser.test.ts`)

| Test Case | Input | Expected |
|-----------|-------|----------|
| Empty string | `""` | Success, null value |
| Simple key-value | `key: value` | Success, {key: "value"} |
| Nested mapping | `a:\n  b: c` | Success, {a: {b: "c"}} |
| Simple sequence | `- a\n- b` | Success, ["a", "b"] |
| Mixed nesting | `items:\n  - a\n  - b` | Success, {items: ["a", "b"]} |
| Quoted strings | `key: "val: ue"` | Success, {key: "val: ue"} |
| Numbers | `count: 42` | Success, {count: 42} |
| Booleans | `flag: true` | Success, {flag: true} |
| Comments | `# comment\nkey: val` | Success, {key: "val"} |
| Inline array | `items: [a, b]` | Success, {items: ["a", "b"]} |
| Inline object | `obj: {a: 1}` | Success, {obj: {a: 1}} |
| Invalid: bad indent | `a:\nb: c` | Error at line 2 |
| Invalid: unclosed quote | `key: "value` | Error at line 1 |
| Invalid: bad colon | `key value` | Error at line 1 |

#### 7.2.2 CLI Integration Tests (`src/validate.test.ts`)

| Test Case | Setup | Expected |
|-----------|-------|----------|
| Valid file | Temp file with valid YAML | Exit 0, success message |
| Invalid file | Temp file with invalid YAML | Exit 1, error with line |
| Missing file | Non-existent path | Exit 1, file not found |
| No arguments | No args | Exit 1, usage message |

### 7.3 Test NOT Designed

| Category | Reason |
|----------|--------|
| Bun file system behavior | Framework testing |
| process.argv parsing | Runtime behavior |
| Console output formatting | Library feature |

---

## 8. Deployment Design

### 8.1 Package.json Changes

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "validate": "bun run src/validate.ts"
  }
}
```

### 8.2 No Build/Deploy Changes

- No compilation step needed (Bun runs TypeScript directly)
- No environment variables required
- No configuration files needed

---

## 9. Documentation Impact

| Type | Target | Section | KB Source | Rationale |
|------|--------|---------|-----------|-----------|
| add | README.md | CLI Commands | N/A | Document new validate command usage |

---

## 10. Design Decisions Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|
| D1 | Parser architecture | Two-phase (lexer + parser) | Cleaner separation, easier error reporting |
| D2 | File structure | New entry point `validate.ts` | Follows existing `index.ts` pattern |
| D3 | Parser module location | `src/yaml-parser.ts` | Follows existing `utils.ts` pattern |
| D4 | Error reporting | Line number only (no column) | Simpler implementation, sufficient for most cases |
| D5 | Result type | Discriminated union | Type-safe success/error handling |
| D6 | Unsupported features handling | Parse error | Clear feedback for users |

---

## Appendix A: YAML Syntax Reference

### Supported Grammar (Simplified BNF)

```
document    := value
value       := scalar | mapping | sequence
scalar      := string | number | boolean | null
mapping     := (key COLON value NEWLINE)+
sequence    := (DASH value NEWLINE)+
key         := string
string      := QUOTE char* QUOTE | unquoted-char+
number      := DIGIT+ (DOT DIGIT+)?
boolean     := 'true' | 'false'
null        := 'null' | '~'
```

### Indentation Rules

- Indentation uses spaces only (tabs are errors)
- Consistent indentation within a block (typically 2 spaces)
- Nested structures must be indented more than parent

# Design Decisions: YAML Validator Command

**Feature ID**: yaml-validator-command
**Created**: 2026-01-22

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Parser architecture | Two-phase (lexer + parser) | Cleaner separation of concerns, easier error reporting with line/column tracking, more maintainable code | Single-pass parser (simpler but harder to debug), Regex-based parsing (error-prone for nested structures) |
| D2 | File structure for CLI | New entry point `src/validate.ts` | Follows existing pattern of `src/index.ts` as entry point, keeps CLI concerns separate from library code | Add to existing `index.ts` (would mix concerns), Subcommand in index.ts (overcomplicates simple project) |
| D3 | Parser module location | `src/yaml-parser.ts` | Follows existing `src/utils.ts` pattern of utility modules, single-file simplicity | `src/parser/` directory (over-engineered for scope), Inline in validate.ts (poor separation) |
| D4 | Error location granularity | Line number only | Sufficient for typical YAML debugging, simpler implementation, column tracking adds complexity with minimal benefit | Line + column (more complex), Character offset only (not user-friendly) |
| D5 | Parser result type | Discriminated union with success field | Type-safe handling of success/error cases, idiomatic TypeScript, clear API contract | Throw exceptions (less explicit control flow), Tuple [data, error] (less type-safe) |
| D6 | Unsupported YAML features | Return parse error | Clear feedback to users about what went wrong, prevents silent failures or unexpected behavior | Silent ignore (confusing), Partial parse (inconsistent behavior) |
| D7 | Test file organization | Co-located with source | Matches existing `utils.test.ts` pattern in the project | Separate `__tests__` directory (different from existing pattern), Single test file (poor organization) |
| D8 | Script registration | Add "validate" script to package.json | Consistent with existing scripts pattern, simple invocation via `bun run validate` | Direct `bun src/validate.ts` (verbose), Binary registration (overkill) |
| D9 | Indentation handling | Spaces only, tabs are errors | YAML spec recommends spaces, simplifies parser, avoids tab/space mixing issues | Support both (complex), Convert tabs to spaces (implicit behavior) |
| D10 | Multi-line string handling | Support literal (\|) and folded (>) | Common YAML feature needed for configuration files, reasonable complexity | Skip multi-line (too limiting), Full block scalar spec (over-engineered) |

## Decision Details

### D1: Two-Phase Parser Architecture

**Context**: Need to implement a custom YAML parser without external dependencies.

**Decision**: Implement parser in two phases - a lexer (tokenizer) that converts input to tokens, followed by a parser that builds the AST from tokens.

**Consequences**:
- Positive: Clear separation between lexical and syntactic analysis
- Positive: Error messages can include precise location information
- Positive: Easier to test each phase independently
- Negative: Slightly more code than a single-pass approach
- Negative: Two passes over the input (minimal performance impact for typical files)

### D3: Single-File Parser Module

**Context**: How to organize the YAML parser code.

**Decision**: Keep all parser code in a single file `src/yaml-parser.ts`.

**Consequences**:
- Positive: Matches existing project pattern (utils.ts)
- Positive: Simple to understand and navigate
- Positive: No complex module dependencies
- Negative: File may grow large for complex parsers
- Mitigation: Scope limited to basic YAML features keeps file manageable

### D5: Discriminated Union Result Type

**Context**: How to communicate parse success/failure to callers.

**Decision**: Use TypeScript discriminated union with `success: boolean` discriminator.

```typescript
type YamlParseResult =
  | { success: true; data: YamlValue }
  | { success: false; error: string; line: number };
```

**Consequences**:
- Positive: Type-safe - compiler ensures both cases handled
- Positive: No exceptions for expected failure cases
- Positive: Error information always available on failure
- Negative: Slightly more verbose than try/catch

### D9: Spaces-Only Indentation

**Context**: YAML allows both spaces and tabs, but mixing causes issues.

**Decision**: Only allow spaces for indentation. Tabs produce a parse error.

**Consequences**:
- Positive: Simplifies parser implementation
- Positive: Consistent with YAML best practices
- Positive: Avoids tab/space mixing bugs
- Negative: Files using tabs will fail (rare in practice)

## Overview

A command-line YAML syntax validator that accepts a file path argument, parses YAML content using a custom-built parser (no external dependencies), and reports success or failure with appropriate error messages and exit codes.

## Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1] - YAML parser has no dependencies on other new components
2. [T2] - CLI entry point depends on parser being complete
3. [T3] - Package.json update depends on CLI entry point

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (Interface dependency: CLI imports and uses parseYaml function)
- T3 -> T2 (Build dependency: Script references validate.ts entry point)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2 -> T3

## Task Breakdown

### Parser Layer

- [ ] **T1**: Implement YAML parser with lexer and parser in `src/yaml-parser.ts` `[complexity:medium]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#31-yaml-parser-module-srcyaml-parserts](design.md#31-yaml-parser-module-srcyaml-parserts)

    **Effort**: 6 hours

    **Acceptance Criteria**:

    - [ ] Lexer tokenizes YAML input into stream of tokens (KEY, COLON, STRING, NUMBER, BOOLEAN, NULL, DASH, brackets, PIPE, GT, NEWLINE, INDENT, DEDENT, EOF)
    - [ ] Parser implements two-phase approach: lexical analysis followed by parsing
    - [ ] Parser maintains state stack with indent level, context (root/mapping/sequence/inline-mapping/inline-sequence), and expectingValue flag
    - [ ] Supports scalar values (strings, numbers, booleans, null)
    - [ ] Supports quoted strings (single and double quotes)
    - [ ] Supports multi-line strings (pipe `|` and folded `>` syntax)
    - [ ] Supports mappings (nested objects with indentation)
    - [ ] Supports sequences (arrays with dash syntax)
    - [ ] Supports inline sequences `[a, b, c]` and inline mappings `{key: value}`
    - [ ] Supports comments (lines starting with `#`)
    - [ ] Returns discriminated union type: `YamlParseSuccess` or `YamlParseError` with line number
    - [ ] Rejects tabs in indentation as errors
    - [ ] Unit tests pass for all cases in design section 7.2.1

### CLI Layer

- [ ] **T2**: Implement CLI entry point in `src/validate.ts` with argument handling and file I/O `[complexity:simple]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#32-cli-entry-point-srcvalidatets](design.md#32-cli-entry-point-srcvalidatets)

    **Effort**: 2 hours

    **Acceptance Criteria**:

    - [ ] Accepts file path as command-line argument via `process.argv`
    - [ ] Displays usage message when no arguments provided: `Usage: bun run validate <file-path>`
    - [ ] Checks file existence before attempting to read
    - [ ] Outputs `Error: File not found: {path}` for non-existent files
    - [ ] Reads file content using Bun built-in fs
    - [ ] Calls `parseYaml(content)` from yaml-parser module
    - [ ] Outputs `Valid YAML: {path}` on successful parse
    - [ ] Outputs `Syntax error at line {N}: {message}` on parse failure
    - [ ] Returns exit code 0 on success, exit code 1 on any failure
    - [ ] Integration tests pass for all cases in design section 7.2.2

### Configuration

- [ ] **T3**: Add validate script to package.json `[complexity:simple]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#81-packagejson-changes](design.md#81-packagejson-changes)

    **Effort**: 15 minutes

    **Acceptance Criteria**:

    - [ ] `scripts` section includes `"validate": "bun run src/validate.ts"`
    - [ ] Running `bun run validate config.yaml` invokes the validator
    - [ ] No new dependencies added to package.json

### User Docs

- [ ] **TD1**: Create documentation for README.md - CLI Commands `[complexity:simple]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#documentation-impact](design.md#documentation-impact)

    **Type**: add

    **Target**: README.md

    - [ ] Documents `bun run validate <file-path>` command usage

    - [ ] Documents exit codes (0 for success, 1 for failure)

## Acceptance Criteria Checklist

From requirements.md:

- [ ] REQ-001: Running `bun run validate config.yaml` passes the file path to the validator
- [ ] REQ-002: Non-existent file paths produce a clear "file not found" error message
- [ ] REQ-003: Parser correctly handles scalars, key-value mappings, lists, nested structures, and comments

- [ ] REQ-005: Invalid YAML produces error message with line number (e.g., "Syntax error at line 15: ...")

- [ ] STORY-004: GIVEN a valid YAML file WHEN the validate command completes THEN the exit code is 0 AND GIVEN an invalid YAML file WHEN the validate command completes THEN the exit code is non-zero

# rp1-eval-project

A minimal Bun project for testing rp1 agent evaluations.

## Scripts

- `bun run dev` - Run the main entry point
- `bun test` - Run tests
- `bun run lint` - Run linter
- `bun run format` - Run formatter
- `bun run validate` - Validate YAML file syntax

## CLI Commands

### YAML Validator

Validates YAML file syntax by parsing the specified file and reporting success or failure.

**Usage:**

```
bun run validate <file-path>
```

**Arguments:**

- `file-path` - Path to the YAML file to validate

**Exit Codes:**

| Code | Description |
|------|-------------|
| 0 | YAML file is valid |
| 1 | Validation failed or error occurred |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Validate a YAML configuration file
bun run validate config.yaml
# Output: Valid YAML: config.yaml

# Validate a file with a syntax error
bun run validate invalid.yaml
# Output: Syntax error at line 15: unexpected token

# Attempt to validate a non-existent file
bun run validate missing.yaml
# Output: Error: File not found: missing.yaml

# Run without arguments (shows usage)
bun run validate
# Output: Usage: bun run validate <file-path>
```

## Structure

```
src/
  index.ts       - Main entry point
  utils.ts       - Utility functions
  validate.ts    - YAML validator CLI
  yaml-parser.ts - Custom YAML parser
```

# Requirements Specification: YAML Validator Command

**Feature ID**: yaml-validator-command
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-01-22

## 1. Feature Overview

A command-line utility that validates YAML file syntax by parsing files specified via command-line arguments. The validator uses a custom-built minimal YAML parser implemented from scratch, ensuring no new external dependencies are added to the project. This tool enables developers to quickly verify that their YAML configuration files are syntactically correct before deployment or further processing.

## 2. Business Context

### 2.1 Problem Statement

Developers working with YAML configuration files need a quick way to validate file syntax without relying on external dependencies. Invalid YAML files can cause runtime errors, deployment failures, or configuration issues that are difficult to debug. Currently, there is no built-in mechanism to validate YAML syntax within the existing toolset.

### 2.2 Business Value

- Reduces debugging time by catching YAML syntax errors early in the development workflow
- Maintains project simplicity by avoiding additional npm dependencies
- Provides developers with immediate feedback on configuration file validity
- Prevents deployment failures caused by malformed YAML files

### 2.3 Success Metrics

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Correctly identifies valid YAML files | 100% accuracy for supported syntax |
| Correctly identifies invalid YAML files | Clear error messaging with line numbers |
| Command execution time | Less than 500ms for typical config files |
| No new dependencies added | Zero new npm packages |

## 3. Stakeholders & Users

### 3.1 User Types

| User Type | Description | Primary Needs |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| Developer | Team members using CLI tools for development workflow | Quick syntax validation, clear error messages, simple invocation |

### 3.2 Stakeholder Interests

| Stakeholder | Interest |
|-------------|----------|
| Development Team | Maintain codebase simplicity, no dependency bloat |
| Project Maintainers | Ensure tool reliability and minimal maintenance burden |

## 4. Scope Definition

### 4.1 In Scope

- Command-line interface accepting file path argument
- Custom YAML parser implementation (no external dependencies)
- Syntax validation (parse success/failure)
- Clear success/failure output messages
- Line number reporting for syntax errors
- Support for common YAML syntax constructs (scalars, mappings, sequences, comments)

### 4.2 Out of Scope

- YAML schema validation (e.g., validating against a JSON Schema)
- YAML linting or style checking
- YAML formatting or pretty-printing
- Multiple file validation in single command
- Stdin input support
- YAML anchors and aliases
- Multi-document YAML files
- Complex YAML features (tags, custom types, binary data)

### 4.3 Assumptions

- Developers have access to the CLI environment (Bun runtime)
- YAML files are encoded in UTF-8
- Target files are single-document YAML files
- Files are of reasonable size (under 10MB)

## 5. Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: File Path Input
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Must Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The command shall accept a file path as a command-line argument |
| Rationale | Developers need to specify which file to validate |
| Acceptance Criteria | Running `bun run validate config.yaml` passes the file path to the validator |

### REQ-002: File Existence Check
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Must Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The command shall verify the specified file exists before attempting validation |
| Rationale | Clear error messaging prevents confusion when files are missing |
| Acceptance Criteria | Non-existent file paths produce a clear "file not found" error message |

### REQ-003: YAML Syntax Parsing
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Must Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The command shall parse YAML content using a custom-built parser without external dependencies |
| Rationale | Project constraint requires no new npm dependencies |
| Acceptance Criteria | Parser correctly handles scalars, key-value mappings, lists, nested structures, and comments |

### REQ-004: Success Output
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Must Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The command shall output a success message when the YAML file is syntactically valid |
| Rationale | Developers need confirmation that validation passed |
| Acceptance Criteria | Valid YAML files produce output indicating success (e.g., "Valid YAML") |

### REQ-005: Error Output with Location
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Must Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The command shall output an error message including line number when syntax errors are detected |
| Rationale | Line numbers help developers quickly locate and fix errors |
| Acceptance Criteria | Invalid YAML produces error message with line number (e.g., "Syntax error at line 15: ...") |

### REQ-006: Exit Codes
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Should Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The command shall return appropriate exit codes (0 for success, non-zero for failure) |
| Rationale | Enables integration with scripts and CI/CD pipelines |
| Acceptance Criteria | Exit code 0 on valid YAML, exit code 1 on invalid YAML or errors |

### REQ-007: No New Dependencies
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Priority | Must Have |
| User Type | Developer |
| Requirement | The implementation shall not add any new npm packages to the project |
| Rationale | Project constraint to maintain minimal dependencies |
| Acceptance Criteria | package.json dependencies remain unchanged after implementation |

## 6. Non-Functional Requirements

### 6.1 Performance Expectations

| Requirement | Target |
|-------------|--------|
| Validation time for files under 100KB | Less than 100ms |
| Validation time for files under 1MB | Less than 500ms |
| Memory usage | Proportional to file size, no memory leaks |

### 6.2 Security Requirements

| Requirement | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| File access | Only read access to specified file path |
| Path traversal | Handle file paths safely without arbitrary file system access |

### 6.3 Usability Requirements

| Requirement | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| Error clarity | Error messages must be human-readable and actionable |
| Help text | Command should provide usage information when invoked incorrectly |
| Output format | Consistent, parseable output format |

### 6.4 Compliance Requirements

None identified for this feature.

## 7. User Stories

### STORY-001: Validate a YAML Configuration File
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Story | As a Developer, I want to validate a YAML configuration file so that I can ensure it will parse correctly before deployment |
| Acceptance | GIVEN a valid YAML file exists at "config.yaml" WHEN I run `bun run validate config.yaml` THEN I see a success message confirming the file is valid |

### STORY-002: Identify Syntax Errors
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Story | As a Developer, I want to see where syntax errors occur so that I can quickly fix malformed YAML |
| Acceptance | GIVEN a YAML file with a syntax error on line 10 WHEN I run the validate command THEN I see an error message indicating the problem at line 10 |

### STORY-003: Handle Missing Files
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Story | As a Developer, I want clear feedback when a file does not exist so that I can correct the file path |
| Acceptance | GIVEN no file exists at "missing.yaml" WHEN I run `bun run validate missing.yaml` THEN I see an error message stating the file was not found |

### STORY-004: Script Integration
| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Story | As a Developer, I want the command to return proper exit codes so that I can use it in automated scripts |
| Acceptance | GIVEN a valid YAML file WHEN the validate command completes THEN the exit code is 0 AND GIVEN an invalid YAML file WHEN the validate command completes THEN the exit code is non-zero |

## 8. Business Rules

| Rule ID | Rule | Rationale |
|---------|------|-----------|
| BR-001 | The validator must use only built-in language features and existing project code | Maintains zero-dependency constraint |
| BR-002 | Syntax validation only; no semantic or schema validation | Keeps scope minimal and implementation simple |
| BR-003 | Single file per invocation | Simplifies implementation and usage |

## 9. Dependencies & Constraints

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| Bun runtime | Runtime | Command executes in Bun environment |
| File system access | System | Read access to validate target files |

### Constraints

| Constraint | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| No new npm dependencies | Implementation must use only existing packages and built-in features |
| Custom parser | YAML parsing must be implemented from scratch |
| Syntax-only validation | No schema or semantic validation required |

## 10. Clarifications Log

| Question | Clarification | Source |
|----------|---------------|--------|
| Who are the target users? | Developers via CLI | User clarification |
| How is input provided? | File path as command argument | User clarification |
| What level of validation? | Syntax only - check if YAML parses correctly | User clarification |
| Which YAML parser to use? | Custom minimal parser implemented from scratch | User clarification |

---

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Defaults

| Decision Point | Choice | Rationale |
|----------------|--------|-----------|
| PRD selection | None | No PRDs found in .rp1/work/prds/ directory |
| KB context | Best-effort without KB | index.md and concept_map.md not found |

## AFK Mode: Inferred Decisions

| Ambiguity | Resolution | Source |
|-----------|------------|--------|
| Supported YAML features | Basic syntax: scalars, mappings, sequences, comments | Conservative default for "simple" validator |
| Error reporting format | Line number with descriptive message | Standard practice for CLI validators |
| Exit code convention | 0 for success, 1 for failure | Unix convention default |
| File size limits | Reasonable files under 10MB | Conservative default assumption |
| Encoding support | UTF-8 only | Most common YAML encoding |
| Multi-document support | Out of scope | "Simple" validator constraint |
| Advanced YAML features | Out of scope (anchors, aliases, tags) | Custom minimal parser constraint |

# Technical Design: YAML Validator Command

**Feature ID**: yaml-validator-command
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-01-22

---

## 1. Design Overview

This design specifies a command-line YAML syntax validator for the rp1-eval-project. The validator accepts a file path argument, parses the YAML content using a custom-built parser, and reports success or failure with appropriate error messages and exit codes.

### High-Level Architecture

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph CLI["CLI Layer"]
        A[validate.ts]
    end

    subgraph Parser["Parser Layer"]
        B[yaml-parser.ts]
    end

    subgraph System["System Layer"]
        C[File System]
        D[Process/Exit]
    end

    A --> B
    A --> C
    A --> D
    B --> E[YamlLexer]
    B --> F[YamlParser]
```

**Design Principles:**
- Single responsibility: Separate CLI handling from parsing logic
- Zero dependencies: All parsing logic implemented from scratch
- Pattern alignment: Follow existing project structure and conventions

---

## 2. Architecture

### 2.1 Component Structure

| Component | File | Responsibility |
|-----------|------|----------------|
| CLI Entry Point | `src/validate.ts` | Argument parsing, file I/O, output formatting |
| YAML Parser | `src/yaml-parser.ts` | Lexical analysis and parsing of YAML content |

### 2.2 Component Interaction

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant CLI as validate.ts
    participant FS as File System
    participant Parser as yaml-parser.ts

    User->>CLI: bun run validate config.yaml
    CLI->>CLI: Parse arguments
    CLI->>FS: Check file exists
    alt File not found
        CLI->>User: Error: File not found
        CLI->>CLI: exit(1)
    end
    CLI->>FS: Read file contents
    CLI->>Parser: parseYaml(content)
    alt Parse success
        Parser->>CLI: { success: true, data }
        CLI->>User: Valid YAML
        CLI->>CLI: exit(0)
    else Parse failure
        Parser->>CLI: { success: false, error, line }
        CLI->>User: Syntax error at line N: message
        CLI->>CLI: exit(1)
    end
```

---

## 3. Detailed Design

### 3.1 YAML Parser Module (`src/yaml-parser.ts`)

The custom YAML parser implements a two-phase approach: lexical analysis followed by parsing.

#### 3.1.1 Supported YAML Syntax

| Syntax Element | Example | Supported |
|----------------|---------|-----------|
| Scalar values | `key: value` | Yes |
| Quoted strings | `key: "value"` or `key: 'value'` | Yes |
| Multi-line strings | `key: \|` or `key: >` | Yes |
| Numbers | `count: 42` | Yes |
| Booleans | `enabled: true` | Yes |
| Null values | `value: null` or `value: ~` | Yes |
| Mappings (objects) | `key:\n  nested: value` | Yes |
| Sequences (arrays) | `- item1\n- item2` | Yes |
| Inline sequences | `items: [a, b, c]` | Yes |
| Inline mappings | `obj: {key: value}` | Yes |
| Comments | `# comment` | Yes |
| Anchors/Aliases | `&anchor`, `*alias` | No |
| Tags | `!tag` | No |
| Multi-document | `---` separator | No |

#### 3.1.2 Parser Interface

```typescript
// Types
interface YamlParseSuccess {
  success: true;
  data: YamlValue;
}

interface YamlParseError {
  success: false;
  error: string;
  line: number;
  column?: number;
}

type YamlParseResult = YamlParseSuccess | YamlParseError;

type YamlValue =
  | string
  | number
  | boolean
  | null
  | YamlValue[]
  | { [key: string]: YamlValue };

// Main function
function parseYaml(content: string): YamlParseResult;
```

#### 3.1.3 Lexer Design

The lexer tokenizes YAML input into a stream of tokens:

```typescript
enum TokenType {
  KEY,           // key identifier before colon
  COLON,         // :
  STRING,        // quoted or unquoted string value
  NUMBER,        // numeric value
  BOOLEAN,       // true/false
  NULL,          // null/~
  DASH,          // - for list items
  LBRACKET,      // [
  RBRACKET,      // ]
  LBRACE,        // {
  RBRACE,        // }
  COMMA,         // ,
  PIPE,          // | for literal block
  GT,            // > for folded block
  NEWLINE,       // line break
  INDENT,        // indentation increase
  DEDENT,        // indentation decrease
  EOF,           // end of file
}

interface Token {
  type: TokenType;
  value: string;
  line: number;
  column: number;
}
```

#### 3.1.4 Parser State Machine

The parser maintains a state stack for handling nested structures:

```typescript
interface ParserState {
  indent: number;       // Current indentation level
  context: 'root' | 'mapping' | 'sequence' | 'inline-mapping' | 'inline-sequence';
  expectingValue: boolean;
}
```

### 3.2 CLI Entry Point (`src/validate.ts`)

#### 3.2.1 Command Interface

```
Usage: bun run validate <file-path>

Arguments:
  file-path    Path to the YAML file to validate

Exit Codes:
  0            YAML file is valid
  1            Validation failed or error occurred
```

#### 3.2.2 CLI Implementation Structure

```typescript
// Main entry point
async function main(): Promise<void> {
  const args = process.argv.slice(2);

  // Validate arguments
  if (args.length === 0) {
    printUsage();
    process.exit(1);
  }

  const filePath = args[0];

  // Check file existence
  if (!await fileExists(filePath)) {
    console.error(`Error: File not found: ${filePath}`);
    process.exit(1);
  }

  // Read file
  const content = await readFile(filePath);

  // Parse YAML
  const result = parseYaml(content);

  // Output result
  if (result.success) {
    console.log(`Valid YAML: ${filePath}`);
    process.exit(0);
  } else {
    console.error(`Syntax error at line ${result.line}: ${result.error}`);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
```

#### 3.2.3 Error Message Formats

| Scenario | Output Format |
|----------|---------------|
| No arguments | `Usage: bun run validate <file-path>` |
| File not found | `Error: File not found: {path}` |
| Valid YAML | `Valid YAML: {path}` |
| Syntax error | `Syntax error at line {N}: {message}` |

### 3.3 Data Model

No persistent data storage required. The parser produces an in-memory representation that is discarded after validation.

---

## 4. Technology Stack

| Layer | Technology | Justification |
|-------|------------|---------------|
| Runtime | Bun | Project standard (existing) |
| Language | TypeScript | Project standard (existing) |
| File I/O | Bun built-in fs | No external dependencies |
| Testing | bun:test | Project standard (existing) |

---

## 5. Implementation Plan

| # | Component | Description | Effort |
|---|-----------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | YAML Parser Core | Implement lexer and parser in `src/yaml-parser.ts` | Medium |
| 2 | CLI Entry Point | Implement `src/validate.ts` with argument handling | Small |
| 3 | Package.json Update | Add "validate" script | Trivial |

---

## 6. Implementation DAG

**Parallel Groups** (tasks with no inter-dependencies):

1. [T1] - YAML parser has no dependencies on other new components
2. [T2] - CLI entry point depends on parser being complete
3. [T3] - Package.json update depends on CLI entry point

**Dependencies**:

- T2 -> T1 (Interface dependency: CLI imports and uses parseYaml function)
- T3 -> T2 (Build dependency: Script references validate.ts entry point)

**Critical Path**: T1 -> T2 -> T3

---

## 7. Testing Strategy

### 7.1 Test Value Assessment

| Test Category | Value | Rationale |
|---------------|-------|-----------|
| Parser unit tests | HIGH | Core business logic - validates YAML syntax |
| CLI integration tests | MEDIUM | Verifies end-to-end behavior |
| Edge case tests | HIGH | YAML has many syntax variations |

### 7.2 Test Plan

#### 7.2.1 Parser Unit Tests (`src/yaml-parser.test.ts`)

| Test Case | Input | Expected |
|-----------|-------|----------|
| Empty string | `""` | Success, null value |
| Simple key-value | `key: value` | Success, {key: "value"} |
| Nested mapping | `a:\n  b: c` | Success, {a: {b: "c"}} |
| Simple sequence | `- a\n- b` | Success, ["a", "b"] |
| Mixed nesting | `items:\n  - a\n  - b` | Success, {items: ["a", "b"]} |
| Quoted strings | `key: "val: ue"` | Success, {key: "val: ue"} |
| Numbers | `count: 42` | Success, {count: 42} |
| Booleans | `flag: true` | Success, {flag: true} |
| Comments | `# comment\nkey: val` | Success, {key: "val"} |
| Inline array | `items: [a, b]` | Success, {items: ["a", "b"]} |
| Inline object | `obj: {a: 1}` | Success, {obj: {a: 1}} |
| Invalid: bad indent | `a:\nb: c` | Error at line 2 |
| Invalid: unclosed quote | `key: "value` | Error at line 1 |
| Invalid: bad colon | `key value` | Error at line 1 |

#### 7.2.2 CLI Integration Tests (`src/validate.test.ts`)

| Test Case | Setup | Expected |
|-----------|-------|----------|
| Valid file | Temp file with valid YAML | Exit 0, success message |
| Invalid file | Temp file with invalid YAML | Exit 1, error with line |
| Missing file | Non-existent path | Exit 1, file not found |

## Appendix A: YAML Syntax Reference

### Supported Grammar (Simplified BNF)

```
document    := value
value       := scalar | mapping | sequence
scalar      := string | number | boolean | null
mapping     := (key COLON value NEWLINE)+
sequence    := (DASH value NEWLINE)+
key         := string
string      := QUOTE char* QUOTE | unquoted-char+
number      := DIGIT+ (DOT DIGIT+)?
boolean     := 'true' | 'false'
null        := 'null' | '~'
```

### Indentation Rules

- Indentation uses spaces only (tabs are errors)
- Consistent indentation within a block (typically 2 spaces)
- Nested structures must be indented more than parent

# Design Decisions: YAML Validator Command

**Feature ID**: yaml-validator-command
**Created**: 2026-01-22

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | Parser architecture | Two-phase (lexer + parser) | Cleaner separation of concerns, easier error reporting with line/column tracking, more maintainable code | Single-pass parser (simpler but harder to debug), Regex-based parsing (error-prone for nested structures) |
| D2 | File structure for CLI | New entry point `src/validate.ts` | Follows existing pattern of `src/index.ts` as entry point, keeps CLI concerns separate from library code | Add to existing `index.ts` (would mix concerns), Subcommand in index.ts (overcomplicates simple project) |
| D3 | Parser module location | `src/yaml-parser.ts` | Follows existing `src/utils.ts` pattern of utility modules, single-file simplicity | `src/parser/` directory (over-engineered for scope), Inline in validate.ts (poor separation) |
| D4 | Error location granularity | Line number only | Sufficient for typical YAML debugging, simpler implementation, column tracking adds complexity with minimal benefit | Line + column (more complex), Character offset only (not user-friendly) |
| D5 | Parser result type | Discriminated union with success field | Type-safe handling of success/error cases, idiomatic TypeScript, clear API contract | Throw exceptions (less explicit control flow), Tuple [data, error] (less type-safe) |
| D6 | Unsupported YAML features | Return parse error | Clear feedback to users about what went wrong, prevents silent failures or unexpected behavior | Silent ignore (confusing), Partial parse (inconsistent behavior) |
| D7 | Test file organization | Co-located with source | Matches existing `utils.test.ts` pattern in the project | Separate `__tests__` directory (different from existing pattern), Single test file (poor organization) |
| D8 | Script registration | Add "validate" script to package.json | Consistent with existing scripts pattern, simple invocation via `bun run validate` | Direct `bun src/validate.ts` (verbose), Binary registration (overkill) |
| D9 | Indentation handling | Spaces only, tabs are errors | YAML spec recommends spaces, simplifies parser, avoids tab/space mixing issues | Support both (complex), Convert tabs to spaces (implicit behavior) |
| D10 | Multi-line string handling | Support literal (\|) and folded (>) | Common YAML feature needed for configuration files, reasonable complexity | Skip multi-line (too limiting), Full block scalar spec (over-engineered) |

## Decision Details

### D1: Two-Phase Parser Architecture

**Context**: Need to implement a custom YAML parser without external dependencies.

**Decision**: Implement parser in two phases - a lexer (tokenizer) that converts input to tokens, followed by a parser that builds the AST from tokens.

**Consequences**:
- Positive: Clear separation between lexical and syntactic analysis
- Positive: Error messages can include precise location information
- Positive: Easier to test each phase independently
- Negative: Slightly more code than a single-pass approach
- Negative: Two passes over the input (minimal performance impact for typical files)

### D3: Single-File Parser Module

**Context**: How to organize the YAML parser code.

**Decision**: Keep all parser code in a single file `src/yaml-parser.ts`.

**Consequences**:
- Positive: Matches existing project pattern (utils.ts)
- Positive: Simple to understand and navigate
- Positive: No complex module dependencies
- Negative: File may grow large for complex parsers
- Mitigation: Scope limited to basic YAML features keeps file manageable

### D5: Discriminated Union Result Type

**Context**: How to communicate parse success/failure to callers.

**Decision**: Use TypeScript discriminated union with `success: boolean` discriminator.

```typescript
type YamlParseResult =
  | { success: true; data: YamlValue }
  | { success: false; error: string; line: number };
```

**Consequences**:
- Positive: Type-safe - compiler ensures both cases handled
- Positive: No exceptions for expected failure cases
- Positive: Error information always available on failure
- Negative: Slightly more verbose than try/catch

### D9: Spaces-Only Indentation

**Context**: YAML allows both spaces and tabs, but mixing causes issues.

**Decision**: Only allow spaces for indentation. Tabs produce a parse error.

**Consequences**:
- Positive: Simplifies parser implementation
- Positive: Consistent with YAML best practices
- Positive: Avoids tab/space mixing bugs
- Negative: Files using tabs will fail (rare in practice)

- [ ] **T1**: Implement YAML parser with lexer and parser in `src/yaml-parser.ts` `[complexity:medium]`

    **Reference**: [design.md#31-yaml-parser-module-srcyaml-parserts](design.md#31-yaml-parser-module-srcyaml-parserts)

    - [ ] Parser maintains state stack with indent level, context (root/mapping/sequence/inline-mapping/inline-sequence), and expectingValue flag
    - [ ] Supports scalar values (strings, numbers, booleans, null)
    - [ ] Supports quoted strings (single and double quotes)
    - [ ] Supports multi-line strings (pipe `|` and folded `>` syntax)
    - [ ] Supports mappings (nested objects with indentation)
    - [ ] Supports sequences (arrays with dash syntax)
    - [ ] Supports inline sequences `[a, b, c]` and inline mappings `{key: value}`
    - [ ] Supports comments (lines starting with `#`)

# rp1-eval-project

A minimal Bun project for testing rp1 agent evaluations.

## Scripts

- `bun run dev` - Run the main entry point
- `bun test` - Run tests
- `bun run lint` - Run linter
- `bun run format` - Run formatter
- `bun run validate` - Validate YAML file syntax

## CLI Commands

### YAML Validator

Validates YAML file syntax by parsing the specified file and reporting success or failure.

**Usage:**

```
bun run validate <file-path>
```

**Arguments:**

- `file-path` - Path to the YAML file to validate

**Exit Codes:**

| Code | Description |
|------|-------------|
| 0 | YAML file is valid |
| 1 | Validation failed or error occurred |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Validate a YAML configuration file
bun run validate config.yaml
# Output: Valid YAML: config.yaml

# Validate a file with a syntax error
bun run validate invalid.yaml
# Output: Syntax error at line 15: unexpected token

# Attempt to validate a non-existent file
bun run validate missing.yaml
# Output: Error: File not found: missing.yaml

# Run without arguments (shows usage)
bun run validate
# Output: Usage: bun run validate <file-path>
```

## Structure

```
src/
  index.ts       - Main entry point
  utils.ts       - Utility functions
  validate.ts    - YAML validator CLI
  yaml-parser.ts - Custom YAML parser
```

input.content:
# Requirements Specification: YAML Validator Command

**Feature ID**: yaml-validator
**Version**: 1.0.0
**Status**: Draft
**Created**: 2026-01-22

## 1. Feature Overview

A command-line utility that validates YAML file syntax and structure, enabling users to verify their YAML files are well-formed before use in configuration, deployment, or data exchange scenarios. The validator must be implemented without introducing any new external dependencies to the project.

## 2. Business Context

### 2.1 Problem Statement

Users working with YAML files need a quick way to validate syntax correctness without relying on external tools or services. Invalid YAML files can cause deployment failures, configuration errors, and debugging time waste. Currently, there is no built-in validation capability in the project.

### 2.2 Business Value

- Reduces time spent debugging malformed YAML files
- Prevents deployment and configuration failures caused by syntax errors
- Provides immediate feedback during development workflows
- Maintains project simplicity by avoiding dependency bloat

### 2.3 Success Metrics

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Validation accuracy | Correctly identifies 100% of YAML syntax errors |
| Response time | Validates files under 1MB in less than 1 second |
| Zero new dependencies | No additions to package.json dependencies |
| User adoption | Command is used in CI/CD or pre-commit workflows |

## 3. Stakeholders & Users

### 3.1 User Types

| User Type | Description | Primary Needs |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| Developer | Team members creating or editing YAML files | Quick syntax validation, clear error messages |
| DevOps Engineer | Personnel managing configuration files | Batch validation, CI/CD integration |
| QA Engineer | Testing team members | Validation as part of test suites |

### 3.2 Stakeholder Interests

| Stakeholder | Interest |
|-------------|----------|
| Project Maintainers | Keep dependency count minimal, maintain code simplicity |
| End Users | Reliable, fast validation with actionable error messages |

## 4. Scope Definition

### 4.1 In Scope

- Validate YAML syntax correctness for single files
- Validate YAML syntax correctness for multiple files (batch mode)
- Report line numbers and positions of syntax errors
- Support standard YAML 1.1/1.2 syntax
- Command-line interface accessible via project scripts
- Exit codes suitable for CI/CD integration (0 for success, non-zero for failure)
- Human-readable error messages

### 4.2 Out of Scope

- Schema validation (validating against a specific YAML schema)
- YAML file repair or auto-correction
- YAML formatting or prettifying
- YAML to JSON or other format conversion
- GUI or web-based interface
- Remote file validation (URLs)
- Streaming validation for very large files

### 4.3 Assumptions

- Bun runtime provides native YAML parsing capabilities or JavaScript-based parsing is sufficient
- Target YAML files are local filesystem files
- Files are encoded in UTF-8
- Maximum practical file size is under 10MB

## 5. Functional Requirements

### REQ-001: Single File Validation
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Developer, DevOps Engineer
**Requirement**: The system shall accept a file path as input and validate the YAML syntax of that file.
**Rationale**: Core functionality needed for basic validation use case.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given a valid YAML file path, when validation is run, then success message is displayed and exit code is 0
- Given an invalid YAML file path, when validation is run, then error message with file path is displayed and exit code is non-zero
- Given a file with invalid YAML syntax, when validation is run, then error details including line number are displayed

### REQ-002: Multiple File Validation
**Priority**: Should Have
**User Type**: DevOps Engineer
**Requirement**: The system shall accept multiple file paths and validate each file, reporting results for all files.
**Rationale**: Batch validation improves efficiency for users managing multiple configuration files.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given multiple file paths, when validation is run, then each file is validated independently
- Given a mix of valid and invalid files, when validation is run, then all results are reported and exit code reflects overall status
- Validation continues through all files even if some fail

### REQ-003: Error Reporting
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: All Users
**Requirement**: The system shall report syntax errors with file name, line number, column position (if available), and a description of the error.
**Rationale**: Detailed error information enables quick identification and resolution of issues.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Error messages include the file path
- Error messages include the line number where the error was detected
- Error messages include a human-readable description of the syntax problem
- Error output is written to stderr

### REQ-004: Exit Code Behavior
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: DevOps Engineer
**Requirement**: The system shall return exit code 0 when all validated files are valid, and a non-zero exit code when any file is invalid or an error occurs.
**Rationale**: Standard exit codes enable integration with CI/CD pipelines and shell scripts.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Exit code 0 when all files pass validation
- Exit code 1 when one or more files fail validation
- Exit code 2 when command-line arguments are invalid or files cannot be read

### REQ-005: Glob Pattern Support
**Priority**: Could Have
**User Type**: DevOps Engineer
**Requirement**: The system should accept glob patterns to match multiple YAML files for validation.
**Rationale**: Simplifies validation of all YAML files in a directory structure.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given a glob pattern like "config/*.yaml", when validation is run, then all matching files are validated
- Given a pattern matching no files, when validation is run, then appropriate message is displayed

### REQ-006: Quiet Mode
**Priority**: Could Have
**User Type**: DevOps Engineer
**Requirement**: The system should support a quiet mode that only outputs errors, suppressing success messages.
**Rationale**: Cleaner output for CI/CD logs and scripted usage.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- Given quiet flag is set and files are valid, when validation is run, then no output is produced
- Given quiet flag is set and files are invalid, when validation is run, then only error messages are output

### REQ-007: No New Dependencies
**Priority**: Must Have
**User Type**: Project Maintainers
**Requirement**: The implementation shall not add any new entries to package.json dependencies or devDependencies beyond what currently exists.
**Rationale**: Explicit constraint from requirements to maintain project simplicity.
**Acceptance Criteria**:
- package.json dependencies section remains unchanged after implementation
- package.json devDependencies section remains unchanged after implementation
- All YAML parsing is done using built-in capabilities or inline code

## 6. Non-Functional Requirements

### 6.1 Performance Expectations

| Metric | Requirement |
|--------|-------------|
| Small files (<100KB) | Validation completes in under 100ms |
| Medium files (100KB-1MB) | Validation completes in under 1 second |
| Large files (1MB-10MB) | Validation completes in under 10 seconds |
| Memory usage | Should not exceed 100MB for files under 10MB |

### 6.2 Security Requirements

- File paths must be validated to prevent path traversal attacks
- Only local filesystem files should be accessible
- No execution of content within YAML files

### 6.3 Usability Requirements

- Error messages should be clear and actionable
- Command syntax should follow common CLI conventions
- Help text should be available via --help flag
- Command should be runnable via npm/bun scripts

### 6.4 Compliance Requirements

- None identified for this feature

## 7. User Stories

### STORY-001: Basic Validation
**As a** developer
**I want** to validate a YAML configuration file
**So that** I can ensure it has correct syntax before using it

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN a YAML file path
- WHEN I run the yaml validator command with the file path
- THEN I see a success message if valid, or detailed error information if invalid

### STORY-002: Pre-commit Validation
**As a** developer
**I want** to validate all YAML files in my project
**So that** I can catch syntax errors before committing code

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN multiple YAML file paths or a glob pattern
- WHEN I run the yaml validator command
- THEN all files are checked and I see a summary of results

### STORY-003: CI Pipeline Integration
**As a** DevOps engineer
**I want** the validator to return proper exit codes
**So that** my CI pipeline can fail builds on invalid YAML files

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN YAML files in a CI pipeline
- WHEN the validator runs
- THEN exit code 0 indicates success, non-zero indicates failure

### STORY-004: Debugging Invalid Files
**As a** developer
**I want** to see line numbers in error messages
**So that** I can quickly locate and fix syntax errors

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- GIVEN a YAML file with a syntax error
- WHEN I run the validator
- THEN the error message includes the line number and error description

## 8. Business Rules

| Rule ID | Rule | Rationale |
|---------|------|-----------|
| BR-001 | Files with .yaml or .yml extensions are treated as YAML files | Standard YAML file extensions |
| BR-002 | Empty files are considered valid YAML | Empty document is valid per YAML spec |
| BR-003 | Files that cannot be read produce file access errors, not validation errors | Distinguishes between access issues and syntax issues |
| BR-004 | Multi-document YAML files (using ---) are supported | Common pattern in Kubernetes and other configs |

## 9. Dependencies & Constraints

### Dependencies

| Dependency | Type | Description |
|------------|------|-------------|
| Bun Runtime | Runtime | Project uses Bun as the JavaScript runtime |
| Filesystem Access | System | Requires read access to target YAML files |

### Constraints

| Constraint | Impact |
|------------|--------|
| No new npm dependencies | Must use built-in parsing or implement YAML parsing inline |
| TypeScript codebase | Implementation should be in TypeScript consistent with project |
| Bun-specific APIs allowed | May use Bun built-in capabilities if available |

## 10. Clarifications Log

| Question | Resolution | Source |
|----------|------------|--------|
| What YAML versions to support? | YAML 1.1 and 1.2 (standard) | Conservative default |
| Should schema validation be included? | No, syntax validation only | Scope constraint for simplicity |
| Maximum file size? | 10MB practical limit | Conservative default for CLI tool |
| Support for stdin input? | Out of scope for initial version | MVP scoping |

---

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Defaults

| Decision Point | Choice | Rationale |
|----------------|--------|-----------|
| PRD selection | None available | No PRDs found in .rp1/work/prds/ |
| KB context | Best-effort without KB | KB files (index.md, concept_map.md) not present |
| Project type | TypeScript/Bun CLI project | Inferred from package.json and src/ structure |

## AFK Mode: Inferred Decisions

| Ambiguity | Resolution | Source |
|-----------|------------|--------|
| "simple" validator scope | Syntax validation only, no schema validation | Conservative interpretation of "simple" |
| "command" interface | CLI command runnable via bun/npm scripts | Project structure shows CLI pattern in index.ts |
| "without adding new deps" | Zero additions to dependencies or devDependencies | Literal interpretation of constraint |
| Target users | Developers and DevOps engineers | Standard users for CLI validation tools |
| Error verbosity | Include line numbers and descriptions | Industry standard for validators |
| Multi-file support | Should Have priority | Common need but not explicitly required |
| YAML version support | 1.1 and 1.2 | Most common versions in use |

# Design Decisions: YAML Validator Command

**Feature ID**: yaml-validator
**Created**: 2026-01-22

## Decision Log

| ID | Decision | Choice | Rationale | Alternatives Considered |
|----|----------|--------|-----------|------------------------|
| D1 | YAML Parsing Approach | Inline syntax validator | REQ-007 mandates no new dependencies; Bun has no built-in YAML parser; inline implementation provides control and meets constraint | External library like js-yaml (rejected - violates no-dependency constraint), Bundled/vendored library (rejected - still counts as dependency code to maintain) |
| D2 | CLI Argument Parsing | Manual process.argv processing | No external dependencies allowed; argument structure is simple (files, --quiet, --help); follows existing pattern in src/index.ts | yargs (rejected - npm dependency), commander (rejected - npm dependency), minimist (rejected - npm dependency) |
| D3 | File Structure | Flat src/ layout with yaml-validator.ts and yaml-parser.ts | Matches existing minimal project structure (utils.ts, index.ts pattern); avoids over-engineering for a 2-module feature | Nested src/yaml-validator/ folder (rejected - overkill for project size), Single file (rejected - poor separation of concerns) |
| D4 | Glob Implementation | Bun.Glob built-in API | Native Bun runtime capability, not an npm package dependency; well-tested implementation | node-glob npm package (rejected - adds dependency), fast-glob (rejected - adds dependency), Manual glob implementation (rejected - unnecessary when Bun provides it) |
| D5 | Error Output Format | stderr with file:line:column: message format | Standard linter/compiler format familiar to developers; easily parsed by IDEs and CI systems; follows Unix convention (errors to stderr) | JSON structured output (rejected - overly complex for CLI use case), Simple text (rejected - less useful for IDE integration) |
| D6 | Multi-file Error Handling | Continue validation, report all errors | Better user experience for batch validation; allows fixing multiple files in one pass; exit code still reflects overall status | Stop on first error (rejected - less useful for batch operations) |
| D7 | Test Framework | bun:test | Existing project test pattern; no additional dependencies; native Bun integration | Jest (rejected - would add devDependency), Vitest (rejected - would add devDependency), Mocha (rejected - would add devDependency) |
| D8 | Validation Scope | Syntax validation only, not schema validation | Explicit in requirements scope; reduces complexity significantly; schema validation would require additional specification | Full YAML parsing (rejected - more complexity than needed), Schema validation (rejected - out of scope per REQ) |
| D9 | Exit Code Strategy | 0=success, 1=validation error, 2=file/arg error | REQ-004 explicitly specifies this; standard Unix convention; allows CI to distinguish error types | Single non-zero for all errors (rejected - less informative), Exit on first error (rejected - loses batch info) |
| D10 | YAML Version Support | YAML 1.1 and 1.2 core syntax | Covers vast majority of YAML files in use; 1.2 is current standard; 1.1 compatibility for legacy files | YAML 1.2 only (rejected - would break some legacy files), Full spec compliance (rejected - extreme complexity for inline impl) |

## AFK Mode: Auto-Selected Technology Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Source | Rationale |
|----------|--------|--------|-----------|
| Runtime | Bun | Codebase analysis | package.json scripts use `bun`, devDependencies include @types/bun |
| Language | TypeScript | Codebase analysis | All source files are .ts, tsconfig.json present |
| Test Framework | bun:test | Codebase analysis | Existing utils.test.ts uses `import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test"` |
| Module System | ES Modules | tsconfig.json | "module": "ESNext", "type": "module" in package.json |
| Strict Mode | Enabled | tsconfig.json | "strict": true already configured |
| File I/O | Bun.file API | Bun runtime default | Native async file API, no dependencies needed |
| Glob Support | Bun.Glob | Bun runtime default | Native glob support, no npm package needed |
| Output Pattern | console.log/console.error | Codebase analysis | Existing index.ts uses console.log for output |
| Argument Access | process.argv | Codebase analysis | Existing index.ts uses process.argv[2] pattern |
| Test Co-location | Same directory as source | Codebase analysis | utils.test.ts alongside utils.ts |

## Risk Decisions

| Risk | Decision | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Inline YAML parser may not handle all edge cases | Accept partial coverage | Document known limitations; focus on common YAML patterns; add tests for edge cases |
| Performance with large files | Accept synchronous processing | File size check before processing; document 10MB limit |
| Security (path traversal) | Implement path validation | Normalize paths; reject URLs; validate within working directory |

## Deferred Decisions

| Topic | Reason | When to Decide |
|-------|--------|----------------|
| stdin input support | Out of scope for v1 | Future enhancement if requested |
| JSON output format | Not in requirements | If CI tools request structured output |
| Watch mode | Not in requirements | If continuous validation requested |
| Config file support | Not in requirements | If default options needed |
